outcome: Unsupported research needs are now born as structured unavailable candidates and later papers reuse that same candidate identity
owner_impact: Research AI now sees implemented support separately from candidate capabilities and candidate contract deltas. A covering candidate collects another paper/Experiment as evidence instead of opening another Professor request; a related but too-narrow candidate is flagged for Professor generalization; only a genuinely absent need creates one new request. Candidates remain unavailable to the compiler, so this does not make any missing scientific capability executable.

next.text: Next is #373, which lets the Professor generalize an existing candidate when later scientific evidence shows its current identity is too narrow. It has not started yet.

technical_evidence: MCP server/interface are 3.12.0 / 16 with capability-request interface vlab.capability-request/7; the nine-tool connector surface and authoring contract vlab.authoring/0.9 are unchanged.

Semantic requests persist a candidate capability with scientific identity, target artifact/runtime domain and concrete authoring surfaces; the other five request classes persist candidate contract deltas against precise stable-contract paths.
Candidate capability keys and candidate contract-delta class/key pairs are unique, and duplicate creation is rejected in favor of evidence reuse.
Evidence links distinguish covered from generalization_needed and the Professor inbox surfaces generalization-needed evidence.
Candidate/request lifecycle state does not make a candidate authorable; only implemented capability bindings and stable implemented contract rules drive compiler acceptance.
No AI matcher, embedding, string-similarity heuristic, capability implementation, simulator runtime change, CI/CD change, retry/timeout change or development-workflow change is introduced.
